treatments.name: Topical Minoxidil 5%
treatments.mechanism: Vasodilator — opens potassium channels in follicle cells, increases blood flow, prolongs anagen (growth) phase
treatments.notes: Foundation treatment. Apply on DRY scalp. Don't wash for 4+ hours.

treatments.name: Microneedling 1.5mm
treatments.mechanism: Creates controlled micro-injuries triggering wound-healing cascade — releases PDGF, VEGF, EGF growth factors. Increases topical absorption by 4×
treatments.notes: Skip minoxidil for 24 hours after needling. Sanitize roller with 70% isopropyl alcohol.

treatments.name: Topical Finasteride 0.1%
treatments.mechanism: Inhibits 5α-reductase Type II locally at the follicle, reducing scalp DHT by ~70% with 100× less blood concentration than oral
treatments.mechanismShort: Blocks DHT at the scalp, not in blood
treatments.evidenceLabel: Phase III RCTs, comparable to oral finasteride
sideEffects: Sexual side effects: 2.8% in Phase III trial (vs 3.3% placebo — not statistically significant)
treatments.notes: Available as Morr-F in India (minoxidil 5% + finasteride 0.1% combo). Once daily is BETTER than twice daily for scalp DHT reduction (70% vs 50%).

treatments.name: Redensyl 3% Serum
treatments.mechanism: Targets hair follicle stem cells (Outer Root Sheath cells) via DHQG + EGCG2 signaling. Reactivates dormant follicles. Different pathway than minoxidil.
treatments.mechanismShort: Activates dormant hair follicle stem cells
treatments.timeToResults: 3 months for density, 4-6 months for thickness
treatments.notes: Works through completely different mechanism than minoxidil — genuine synergy, not overlap. Look for products with 3% concentration. Anagain + Baicapil combos are even better.

treatments.name: Ketoconazole 2% Shampoo
treatments.mechanism: Antifungal with mild anti-androgenic and anti-inflammatory action at the scalp surface
treatments.mechanismShort: Scalp health + mild local DHT reduction
treatments.notes: Leave on for 3-5 minutes before rinsing. Use sulfate-free shampoo on other days.

treatments.name: Saw Palmetto 320mg
treatments.mechanism: Natural 5α-reductase inhibitor — reversible, weak binding. Reduces serum DHT by ~30% without affecting neurosteroid production
sideEffects: Zero sexual side effects in all trials
treatments.notes: Use lipid-standardized extract. Unlike finasteride, binding is reversible and too weak to affect neurosteroids.

treatments.name: Pumpkin Seed Oil 400mg
treatments.mechanism: 5α-reductase inhibition via phytosterols (beta-sitosterol). Antioxidant fatty acids support follicle health.
treatments.evidenceLabel: RCT: 40% hair count increase at 24 weeks
treatments.notes: The clinical study used 400mg of concentrated oil extract — NOT the same as eating pumpkin seeds (different phytosterol concentration).

treatments.name: Rosemary Oil (Topical)
treatments.mechanism: Improves microcirculation to scalp + mild 5α-reductase inhibition. Similar mechanism to minoxidil.
treatments.notes: Overlaps with minoxidil's mechanism (both are vasodilators) — not recommended when already using minoxidil. Better for people NOT using minoxidil.

treatments.name: Oral Finasteride 1mg
treatments.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits 5α-reductase Type II systemically. Reduces serum DHT by ~70%.
treatments.evidenceLabel: FDA-approved, decades of data, gold standard
sideEffects: Sexual side effects: ~5% in meta-analysis (vs ~3% placebo)
treatments.notes: Most effective single treatment for AGA. ~5% sexual side effect rate in meta-analysis (vs ~3% placebo). Most side effects resolve on discontinuation. Nocebo effect contributes significantly to reported rates.

treatments.name: Oral Minoxidil 2.5mg
treatments.mechanism: Systemic vasodilator — reaches ALL follicles evenly. Originally a blood pressure medication used off-label.
treatments.mechanismShort: Systemic growth stimulation, faster than topical
treatments.timeToResults: Faster than topical — visible at 2-3 months
treatments.notes: Not FDA-approved for hair loss. Requires BP monitoring. More effective than topical but with systemic cardiovascular considerations.

treatments.name: GHK-Cu Copper Peptide
treatments.mechanism: Naturally occurring tripeptide that activates dermal papilla cells, promotes angiogenesis, anti-inflammatory, stimulates collagen
treatments.evidenceLabel: Promising preclinical + case studies, limited large RCTs
treatments.notes: Best used after microneedling for enhanced penetration. Synergistic with microneedling.

treatments.name: PRP (Platelet Rich Plasma)
treatments.mechanism: Concentrated growth factors from your own blood injected into scalp. Delivers PDGF, VEGF, TGF-β, IGF directly to follicles.
treatments.mechanismShort: Your own blood's growth factors, concentrated
treatments.evidenceLabel: Multiple RCTs show improved density and thickness
sideEffects: None systemic — it's your own blood
treatments.applicationFrequency: Monthly for 4-6 sessions, then every 3-6 months
treatments.notes: In-clinic procedure. Cost: ₹4,000-10,000 per session (India). Best as add-on to a base protocol.

treatments.name: Low-Level Laser Therapy (LLLT)
treatments.mechanism: Red/near-infrared light (650-670nm) stimulates mitochondria in follicle cells → increased ATP → cell proliferation
treatments.notes: Modest standalone benefit. Better as adjunct. Home devices: iRestore, HairMax, Theradome.

treatments.name: Anagain (Pea Sprout Extract)
treatments.mechanism: Stimulates dermal papilla cells, upregulates FGF7 and noggin gene expression for hair growth initiation
treatments.mechanismShort: Dermal papilla activation via pea sprout extract
treatments.applicationFrequency: Daily (usually combined with Redensyl in serums)
treatments.notes: Most effective when combined with Redensyl and Baicapil in multi-active serums.

treatments.name: Baicapil
treatments.mechanism: Botanical blend (Scutellaria baicalensis + wheat sprouts + soy sprouts) that activates follicle stem cells and reduces oxidative stress
treatments.evidenceLabel: 22% hair density increase, 60% hair fall reduction
treatments.notes: Best evidence is for telogen effluvium. For AGA, best used as an adjunct in multi-active serums.

treatments.name: Topical Caffeine
treatments.mechanism: PDE inhibitor that stimulates follicle proliferation and counteracts testosterone-induced growth suppression in vitro
treatments.mechanismShort: Follicle stimulant, counteracts testosterone in vitro
treatments.evidenceLabel: In vitro evidence, limited human RCTs
treatments.notes: Weak evidence as standalone. Often included as a supporting ingredient in multi-active serums.

treatments.name: DIM (Diindolylmethane)
treatments.mechanism: Promotes healthy estrogen metabolism — converts strong estrogens to weaker forms. Counteracts testosterone-to-estradiol aromatization.
treatments.notes: Primarily a finasteride shield supplement. Most useful when taking finasteride to counteract the testosterone→estradiol aromatization pathway.

treatments.name: Ashwagandha (KSM-66)
treatments.mechanism: Adaptogen that increases testosterone (14-40%), reduces cortisol (30%), improves GABA activity, enhances sexual function
treatments.evidenceLabel: Multiple RCTs for testosterone and cortisol
treatments.notes: Primarily a finasteride shield supplement. Supports testosterone and GABA pathways that finasteride can impact.
